timeline.title: Company sections mark the township's land grants
timeline.body: Under the 1870 transfer of Rupert's Land, Section 8 of the Moosomin township went to the Hudson's Bay Company, and Section 7 to the Canada North West Land Company. The Canadian Pacific Railway Company became the township's largest grantee, with 35 quarters.

timeline.title: Treaty 4 signed; townsite at a trail junction
timeline.body: Moosomin lies in Treaty 4 territory, the Qu'Appelle Treaty signed in 1874. The townsite was located where Hudson's Bay Company trails between Fort Pelly, Fort Ellice and the Moose Mountain reserves met. A North-West Mounted Police detachment under Sergeant Norris was on the ground in the earliest days.

timeline.label: c. 1881
timeline.title: First settlers arrive ahead of the railway
timeline.body: Settlers, mostly of English and Scottish origin, began arriving around 1881, before the railway reached the site. The earliest years were shaped by the Canadian Pacific Railway construction camps pushing the roadbed west.

timeline.title: Town named for Chief Moosomin or the mooseberry
timeline.body: Accounts give two possible origins for the name: Cree Chief Moosomin, who signed Treaty 6 at Battleford in 1880, or the Cree word mosomin, meaning mooseberry (high bush cranberry). The sources note the two accounts are compatible, since the chief was himself named for the berry.

timeline.title: Founded as Siding No. 4 with the CPR's arrival
timeline.body: With the arrival of the Canadian Pacific Railway in 1882, the community began as Siding No. 4, later called the Moosomin Station. It is described as the first Saskatchewan community founded on steel. A large CPR construction camp with canvas boarding houses stayed on as the base for pushing the line west.

timeline.label: Fall 1882
timeline.title: Post office opens and McNaughton's store anchors town
timeline.body: The post office was established in the fall of 1882. R. D. McNaughton, the first merchant to arrive, opened the general store that anchored the early settlement. The village was incorporated the same year.

timeline.label: May 1884
timeline.title: Baroness Burdett-Coutts colony brings London families
timeline.body: A colony backed by the Baroness Burdett-Coutts brought 18 families from London's East End in May 1884 to settle south and east of Moosomin.

timeline.title: Saskatchewan's first commercial elevator built
timeline.body: The Ogilvie Elevator Company built the first commercial grain elevator in Saskatchewan at Moosomin in 1884. It marked the start of grain handling on the new rail line.

items.title: Hudson's Bay and land-company sections frame the township
items.body: Two whole sections went to companies rather than settlers.
items.source: Library and Archives Canada, Land Grants of Western Canada, 1870-1930

items.title: Town named Moosomin
items.body: Named for Chief Moosomin or the mooseberry.

items.title: Cenotaph unveiled before 3,000 people
items.body: Moosomin's cenotaph was unveiled on August 31, 1924, by acting Lieutenant-Governor Sir Frederick Haultain before an estimated 3,000 people. The $4,000 monument featured a bronze soldier modelled in Carrara and cast in Florence, Italy, shipped across the Atlantic on the S.S. Colombo. The site had been a water-filled pothole, filled by some 800 wagonloads of volunteer earth; Victoria Cross winners Major Allard and Sgt. Harry Mullin were among those present.

items.title: Queen's Hotel fire kills three
items.body: Unverified: in January 1969 the Grosvenor section of the Queen's Hotel burned, and three residents died. The account comes from a detailed specialist blog drawing on the hotel family's recollections but is otherwise single-source and needs checking before print.
